propositions: Attribute-form git wrapper calls (e.g., core._git(...)) are already detected by the ast.Attribute branch in _wrapper_name, but this behavior is untested and undocumented, making it appear absent.
All 8 existing R2 tests in test_raw_git_write_lint.py exercise only bare-name form (ast.Name), leaving attribute-form detection vulnerable to accidental deletion in future refactors.
_ref_lock_push.py has no gate hits not because attribute calls escape, but because push is not in MUTATION_VERBS; the call is seen and resolved correctly but does not fire as intended.
The gate's module docstring must explicitly state that wrapper detection matches by the callable's attribute name regardless of receiver shape, so attribute-form coverage is no longer implicit.
Four new tests must pin attribute-form detection: literal mutation verb firing, receiver-shape independence, opaque-argv fail-closed behavior, and marker-silencing on the attribute form.
